'''Patricia F. Campbell''' is an American mathematician and [[mathematics education|mathematics educator]]. She is a professor in the Department of Teaching and Learning, Policy and Leadership at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://education.umd.edu/directory/patricia-f-campbell|title=Patricia F. Campbell|work=College of Education Directory|publisher=University of Maryland|accessdate=2019-06-30|archive-date=2019-06-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190630193159/https://education.umd.edu/directory/patricia-f-campbell|url-status=dead}}</ref> Her work has concerned the improvement of mathematics education in minority and lower-income secondary schools,<ref name=hay/> and the effectiveness of mathematics coaching in mathematics education.

Campbell is a graduate of the [[University of St. Francis|College of St. Francis]]. After earning a master's degree in mathematics at [[Michigan State University]], she completed a Ph.D. in mathematics education at the [[Florida State University]].<ref name=cv>{{citation|url=https://education.umd.edu/file/1798/download?token=nYfEzPb5|title=Curriculum vitae|accessdate=2019-08-20|archive-date=2019-08-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190820234848/https://education.umd.edu/file/1798/download%3Ftoken%3DnYfEzPb5|url-status=dead}}</ref> She was co-chair of the [[American Educational Research Association]] Special Interest Group on Research in Math Education for 2007–2009.<ref>{{citation|url=http://sigrme.org/sig-officers/past-sig-officers/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171102164830/http://sigrme.org/sig-officers/past-sig-officers/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=November 2, 2017|title=Past SIG Officers|publisher=Special Interest Group on Research in Math Education|accessdate=2019-11-02}}</ref>

In 2011 she was given the Twenty-First Annual [[Louise Hay Award]] for Contributions to Mathematics Education. The [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] awarded it to her "for her contributions to the teaching and learning of mathematics in urban settings and for working in schools that serve predominantly minority populations from low-income backgrounds".<ref name=hay>{{citation|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/hay-award/hay-award-2011/|title=Louise Hay Award, 2011 Winner: Patricia Campbell|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|accessdate=2019-06-30}}</ref>
